text: The Patriots got some crucial roster relief this week with the activation of A.J. Brown from injured reserve after his four-game absence due to a right high ankle sprain, though the star receiver's actual availability for Sunday's divisional clash with the Jets remains genuinely uncertain—Brown himself acknowledged his status is "still up in the air" despite returning to practice, leaving Mike Vrabel's decision pending until Saturday. The team also elevated safety Elliott Davison from the practice squad while cornerstone cornerback Christian Gonzalez is expected to play, setting up what the Jets clearly view as a pivotal game (Garrett Wilson called it a "big-ass game" for New York's divisional aspirations), and there's legitimate intrigue in how the Patriots might capitalize on momentum from their dominant 28-point win last week against a Geno Smith-led Jets offense that's arrived in New England riding an impressive interception-free streak. Beyond the field, tight end Hunter Henry earned NFLPA Community MVP honors for the week after hosting the second annual "Freedom to Play" ping pong tournament, continuing a streak that saw teammate Mack Hollins receive the same recognition just two weeks prior. The football world also mourned the passing of Jon Morris, the legendary center who spent 11 of his 15 professional seasons with the Patriots organization during his storied AFL and NFL career.
